meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of class, so that apology is for the wrong person. What do you have that justifies the zero?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing that down, Hale. Show me the note you made on November 2, with the date on it. Then tell me whether that was the only time Owen was asked about his essay before the zero went in.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale. That's called revising. Put the October 15 outline and the essay in front of me, and I'll read both myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Hale, you're asking Owen to sit a rewrite Thursday morning and giving me the terms on Friday afternoon, which is backwards. I'm writing that down. I still haven't seen the note or the outline, so the zero comes out of the gradebook today and the terms are in my inbox before Thursday.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook today, the terms of any rewrite in writing before Thursday, and the November 2 note and the October 15 outline set beside the essay for me to read. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn today and the terms in writing before Thursday, with the note and the outline put in front of her.
What moved her: owning the zero going in before the call in one sentence got a flat okay, and the dated detail about the November 2 question and the October 15 outline got her taking notes, because she could check both.
What cost ground: offering the rewrite and its terms before showing her a single document, with the written terms arriving only after the rewrite, made it sound like a deal being pushed on her.
Try next time: when she asks for the November 2 note, hand it over right then along with the outline and the essay, and only talk terms once she has read them.
